Author’s note:

In my first year as a PhD student, the institute (Acoustics and audio institutes, part 1: the Institute of Technical Acoustics (ITA), RWTH Aachen) held its Christmas party. An old man sat down across from me. Our eyes met, and he introduced himself with great warmth:

— Ich bin Heinrich Kuttruff. Wie heißen Sie? (I’m Heinrich Kuttruff. What’s your name?)

— Bitte? (Sorry?)

The old man stood up and leaned in a little closer:

— Ich bin Heinrich Kuttruff. Wie heißen Sie?

— Ah OK. Ich bin xxx. (Oh, right. I’m xxx.)

What went through my head was: who is this old guy? Never heard of him!

Only later did I find out that this was the famous Heinrich Kuttruff, the doctoral advisor of my own advisor (Giants of acoustics, part 1: Michael Vorländer). I had been sitting across from a legend and failed to recognize him.

The old professor was nearly 90 by then, yet so full of energy you would never have guessed it. In those years he came to the institute’s Christmas party every year, and every so often he would drive himself to the institute library to look things up for the sixth edition of his book. Whenever we ran into each other we would exchange a few words. Later he came to fewer and fewer of the institute’s events, and I seldom saw him. The next news I had of him was of his death last year.

I have always believed that academia suits only one kind of person: people like Professor Kuttruff, for whom scholarship is a lifelong hobby. Only people like that belong in academia, and only people like that can make disruptive changes.

Professor Karl Heinrich Kuttruff, a grand master of acoustics and one of the founders of modern room acoustics, died in Aachen, Germany, on September 15, 2024, at the age of 94.

His life

Professor Karl Heinrich Kuttruff was born in Germany on August 17, 1930.

Growing up in postwar Germany, the young Kuttruff already showed a keen interest in physics and acoustics. He studied at leading German universities, specializing in acoustics and architectural acoustics under several of the field’s leading authorities. Those years laid a solid foundation for his later achievements.

Academic career

  • 1956: PhD in physics, RWTH Aachen University

  • 1959–1963: Research assistant, RWTH Aachen University

  • 1963: Habilitation

  • 1965: Appointed professor at the Institute of Technical Acoustics, RWTH Aachen University

  • 1965–1995: Head of the Institute of Technical Acoustics at RWTH Aachen University, where he built world-class acoustics research facilities

  • 1995: Retired and was named professor emeritus of RWTH Aachen University

Over his long tenure he built world-class research facilities and trained a great many outstanding acousticians, making a major contribution to the development of the field.

Research contributions

Theory

  • Pioneered the development of statistical room acoustics

  • Proposed new models of sound scattering to solve complex problems in room acoustics

  • Brought numerical simulation into acoustics research

Practice

  • Developed new acoustic measurement methods and standards

  • Designed innovative acoustic laboratory equipment and test systems

  • Established scientific criteria for evaluating acoustic materials

  • Provided acoustic optimization for many concert halls

Books

The classics

Room Acoustics

  • First published in 1973, now in its sixth edition

  • Known as the “bible” of room acoustics

  • Translated into many languages

  • Essential reading for anyone studying acoustics

Acoustics: An Introduction

  • A systematic grounding in theory for newcomers to acoustics

  • Widely praised around the world

Papers

  • Hundreds of high-quality research papers

  • Several of them regarded as milestones in acoustics

  • Widely cited and studied

Honors

Awards

  • Lifetime achievement award of the German Acoustical Society

  • Honorary member of the European Acoustics Association

  • Awards for outstanding contributions from several international acoustics organizations

Influence

  • Regarded as one of the founders of modern room acoustics

  • Trained a great many outstanding acousticians

  • Advanced the internationalization of acoustics standards

  • Made important contributions to acoustics education
